book.duplicateIsbn: That ISBN already exists in the library

shelves.adminOnly: Changing shelf structure needs the admin password
shelves.positionHint: Only drives the 2D map today, but the same coordinates will carry over to a DXF floor plan later
shelves.heightHint: Clear height between shelf boards — decides how tall a book can go in
shelves.deleteBookcaseConfirm: Deleting this bookcase also deletes all of its levels. Continue?
shelves.noLevels: This bookcase has no levels yet
shelves.bodySizeHint: Drives the footprint on the plan and the 3D model; each level's own width is set per level

shelves.transferHint: The bookcase lands in the roomiest spot of the target room. The books on it are untouched.
shelves.elevationHint: Level width {width}mm · body height {height}mm · {levels} levels — drawn to true scale
shelves.deleteBookcaseHasBooks: This bookcase holds {count} book(s). They will become unshelved and need reshelving one by one (the books themselves are kept). Delete anyway?
shelves.deleteLevelHasBooks: This level holds {count} book(s). They will become unshelved and need reshelving (the books themselves are kept). Delete anyway?

tags.title: Tags
tags.hint: Plain categories are enough: fiction, history, textbooks, magazines… no need for a library classification scheme
tags.name: Name
tags.deleteConfirm: Delete this tag? The books themselves are kept.
tags.zonesHint: Assign a tag to specific levels so the system can warn you when that category is running out of room
tags.totalWidth: Total width of books with this tag
tags.usageTitle: How do you use this book?
tags.usageHint: These tags change **how high it gets shelved**: reading / to-read / often-used go within easy reach; lent-out gives up the golden zone. The classification cannot express this — only you know it.
tags.usageRare: Gives up the golden zone; may go higher

capacity.title: Space check
capacity.needsConfirmHint: The maths lands in the borderline range, so the system will not decide. Go look at the shelf — if it goes in, tap 'It fits'.
capacity.noSuggestion: No suitable level. You may need to add one, or move other books out first.
capacity.migrationBody: Books tagged '{tag}' total {total} mm, but the assigned levels only offer {allocated} mm — over by {overflow} mm.
capacity.migrationOptionNewLevel: Assign another level to this tag
capacity.migrationOptionMove: Move the whole tag to a wider level

ai.insufficient: Not enough information available to write a description
ai.insufficientHint: The model has no reliable information about this book, so it did not invent any. Write your own if you like.
ai.onlyWhenEmpty: Only needed when no data source supplied a description

auth.required: This step needs the admin password
auth.whyHint: Adding, deleting and shelving books need no password. Only editing shelf structure does, so the capacity maths cannot be knocked off by accident.

settings.title: Settings
settings.languageHint: Affects interface text only — the language of the book data itself is untouched
settings.coefficientsHint: Spine thickness is estimated from the page count. If estimates run consistently high or low, tune it here.
settings.defaultSpine: Default thickness with no page count (mm)
settings.tightThresholdHint: When free space and estimated thickness are this close, it is handed to you to confirm
settings.levelMargin: Margin left at each end of a level (mm)
settings.backupHint: Export the database and uploaded covers
settings.assumedHeightHint: No data source supplies book dimensions. When a level's clear height exceeds this, unknown book height stops being flagged; below it, you get asked to confirm.

errors.levelDimensionsRequired: Width and height are required and must be greater than 0
errors.rateLimited: Too many requests — try again in {minutes} min. (This guards the public URL against abuse.)
errors.offlineHint: Shelf positions change daily, so showing you cached data would just send you to the wrong shelf. Reconnect and it'll load.
errors.loadFailedHint: The server didn't answer. Give it a moment and try again.
errors.goneAlready: That record is gone — someone may have just deleted it. Try refreshing.
errors.stillReferenced: Something still refers to it; unlink that first
errors.badBody: The request didn't arrive intact — please try again (usually a flaky connection)

callNumber.unsure: Could not determine a class — enter one yourself
callNumber.inferredNote: Inferred, so not necessarily right. Reclassify or type your own.
callNumber.precisionNote: Inferred numbers only go to division level (e.g. I247, not I247.57) — extra decimals would look precise without being so.

place.title: Put it here
place.diagramHint: The yellow level is the target; the arrow shows height above the floor
place.tightTitle: This shelf may not have room
place.tightHint: Only {mm}mm would be left — borderline. Thickness is estimated from page count, so it's approximate. Your call.
place.tooTallTitle: This book is taller than the shelf
place.tooTallHint: About {mm}mm too tall to stand upright. Unless you plan to lay it flat, pick another shelf.

floorplan.title: Floor plan
floorplan.noneHint: Upload a DXF and your bookcases can sit at their real positions on the plan.
floorplan.dragHint: Drag a bookcase to reposition it on the plan (millimetre coordinates, saved automatically)
floorplan.parseFailed: No geometry could be parsed from this DXF
floorplan.deleteConfirm: Delete the floor plan? Bookcase coordinates are kept.

scene.title: 3D space
scene.dragHint: Drag to orbit · click a room to enter
scene.clickRoom: Click a room to step inside
scene.pageHint: {rooms} rooms · {shelves} bookcases · drag to orbit, click a room to step in

rooms.title: Rooms
rooms.hint: Detected from the floor plan. Name them — the names appear in the directory path.
rooms.noneDetected: No closed areas matching room criteria in this plan
rooms.summary: {count} rooms · {area} m² total · {empty} with no bookcase yet
rooms.clickToRename: Click a room to rename it

reflow.title: Reshelving
reflow.hint: Only suggests moves when something genuinely will not fit, and always moves the smallest group. Nothing happens without your click.
reflow.allGoodHint: No overflowing levels — nothing needs moving.
reflow.noSpace: No room anywhere else — add a level or take some books out first.
reflow.planHint: Move all {count} books of “{topic}” together (the smallest group, so the least carrying)
reflow.fillTargetNote: Library practice is 70–75% full; the slack is what makes day-to-day shelving possible.
reflow.undoPartial: Reverted {reverted}; {skipped} could not go back — the level they came from no longer exists. Those stayed where they were moved to; reshelve them manually.

shelving.emptyLevel: empty — can start a new class

inventory.title: Inventory
inventory.hint: Pick a level, then scan the books on it one by one. No need to do the whole house — stop any time.
inventory.pickFirstHint: Once chosen you can start scanning that shelf.
inventory.newBook: new book — add it on the scan page
inventory.scannedCount: Scanned {seen} this round; the system records {total} on this shelf
inventory.allAccounted: Everything accounted for — no stale records
inventory.missingHint: Usually lent out, moved to another room, or gone. Leaving them makes this shelf look fuller than it is, which skews capacity and every placement suggestion.

layout.title: Whole-house plan
layout.hint: Re-plan every shelf in call-number order to see the ideal layout. This is a preview only — nothing moves until you apply it.

effortHint.rebuild: Ignores where things are now and computes the ideal layout. The most moves — for a one-off big clear-out.
effortHint.tidy: Only moves things where it clearly pays, and prefers moving the smaller group. Use this day to day.
effortHint.minimal: Only places new books and genuine overflow; leaves settled shelves alone.

layout.applyHint: You can undo this in one click from the Tidy-up tab.
layout.exceptionsHint: When the shelves are tight something has to give. These are deliberate trade-offs, not oversights.

exception.out_of_reach: out of reach for its reader

reason.no_capacity: no space left in the house

layout.mergesHint: These shelves hold classes too small to fill a shelf on their own, so they were combined. Listed here so the shelf holds no surprises.

insert.shiftHint: To keep the order intact, {count} book(s) shift along:
insert.needsReview: The call-number slot can't absorb this book

reason.budget_exceeded: too many books would have to move — check Tidy up › Whole-house plan
reason.ran_out_of_shelves: every shelf from here on is full; there is nowhere left to push
reason.too_tall: taller than any shelf that could take it

calibrate.title: Calibrate spine estimates
calibrate.hint: Measure how much width the books on one shelf actually take, and the system solves for millimetres-per-page. The whole capacity model rests on that number; two or three shelves is enough.
calibrate.needMore: Not enough to fit yet ({samples} shelves / {books} books; need at least 2 and 10)
calibrate.implausible: These measurements don't fit a plausible coefficient, so the current values are kept. Usually one shelf was mis-measured, or it holds something that isn't a book.
calibrate.clearConfirm: Clear every recorded measurement? The coefficients stay as they are.
calibrate.errEmpty: That shelf has no books on it yet
calibrate.errTooWide: The measured width exceeds the shelf's own width — worth double-checking

labels.title: Print spine labels
labels.hint: Put the call number on the book. While it only exists on screen, you can't tell at the shelf whether the row is still in order, or where the book in your hand belongs.
labels.scopeAll: All books with a call number
labels.tip: In the browser's print dialog keep margins at default and scale at 100%, or the sizes won't match.
labels.missingNumber: {count} more have no call number yet — classify them first.
labels.nothing: Nothing to print in this range.

setup.title: Still missing
setup.hint: None of these are errors, but some features are half-blind until they're done. Each one disappears as you finish it; the whole panel goes when they're all done.

bookcaseSize.what: {count} bookcases have neither dimensions nor shelves
bookcaseSize.why: The plan and 3D can only guess 800×300. Once shelves are entered the body size is derived — no need to measure the carcass separately.

roomNames.what: {count} rooms are still called “房间 N”
roomNames.why: The directory path reads “Room 7 › bookcase › shelf 2”, which tells you nothing about where it is.

floorPlan.why: Without one there are no rooms, no plan view and no 3D — bookcases are just names.

unshelved.why: Unshelved books don't appear on the shelf map, and the whole-house plan can't reserve space for them.

calibrate.why: Every capacity number rests on this coefficient: fill ratios, "will it fit", the nearly-full warning. The default assumes 80gsm paper and real stock varies by nearly half — the same 1m shelf could hold 33 books or 48. Measuring two shelves takes ten seconds each.

shelfFull.what: Shelves are nearly full — room for about {count} more
shelfFull.why: Beyond this, adding a book starts requiring already-shelved books to move (the fuller it gets, the more move). Adding a bookcase now is far less work than reorganising later.

shelfFullRough.what: Shelves are nearly full — room for roughly {count}–{upper} more
shelfFullRough.why: The range is wide because most spine widths are estimated from page count, not measured — the default assumes 80gsm paper and real stock varies by nearly half. Measuring two shelves with a tape takes ten seconds and pins down this number and every fill figure.

backupFailed.why: The nightly job restores each fresh dump to verify it; this one didn't match. You currently have no backup you can trust.

backupStale.why: The scheduled job probably isn't running at all — more insidious than a failure, because nothing reports an error.

derivedDrift.what: Derived fields don't match their source
derivedDrift.why: Sort keys have drifted from classifications, so shelf placement gives wrong answers while the interface looks normal.

authLockout.what: Someone is guessing the admin password ({n})
authLockout.why: Blocked and temporarily locked out. If that wasn't you mistyping, change the password in Settings.

pullStale.what: The off-site copy is {n} days old
pullStale.why: Server backups sit on the same disk as the database — one failure loses both. The copy on the Mac is the one that saves you: run deploy/pull-backup.sh, or check whether that Mac's nightly job has stopped.
